MSFT.rationale: MSFT presents a strong fundamental case: Q3 FY2026 revenue grew 18.3% YoY to $82.89B, EPS grew 23.4% to $4.27, and operating cash flow surged 26% to $46.68B (56% OCF/revenue conversion). The balance sheet is a fortress with ~$38B net cash and negligible debt-to-equity of 0.119. Azure is accelerating at ~40% growth, outpacing AWS, and the AI business has reached a $37B annual run rate (up 123% YoY). Critically, the market is offering this at a PE of 29.82x — 27% below the October 2025 peak of 40.76x — meaning the stock is materially cheaper despite stronger earnings power. The valuation discount to own-history is the central re-rating opportunity. Offsetting factors cap the score below +0.5: (1) the $190B 2026 capex plan (vs $154.6B consensus) with $25B attributed to component inflation creates margin uncertainty — gross margin has already compressed ~140bp over three quarters and FCF margin reportedly dropped to 19.1%; (2) rising 10Y yields at 4.57% compress the earnings-yield spread and limit multiple re-expansion; (3) active UK CMA, FTC, and EU regulatory probes add tail risk to bundling and pricing power. The OpenAI IPO optionality (potential $228B+ stake value) is real but contingent and speculative. Ackman's initiation at ~21x forward earnings provides a credible institutional anchor, but Gates Foundation's complete exit and Third Point's full divestment signal mixed smart-money positioning. Net: excellent franchise at a meaningful discount to history, tempered by capex-driven margin compression risk and rate headwinds.
key_factors: Q3 FY2026 revenue $82.89B, +18.3% YoY; EPS $4.27, +23.4% YoY — accelerating growth trajectory
Operating cash flow $46.68B in Q3, +26% YoY, 56% OCF/revenue conversion — exceptional cash generation
PE diluted at 29.82x, 27% below October 2025 peak of 40.76x, in lower quartile of 365-day range (25.4x–42.8x)
EV/EBIT at 22.59x, 30% below peak of 32.43x — valuation compressed alongside improving fundamentals
Azure grew ~40% in Q3, outpacing AWS (~19%) and narrowing the cloud infrastructure market share gap (Azure ~21-24% vs AWS ~28-30%)
AI business at $37B annual run rate, +123% YoY; Copilot adoption at only 4.4% of 450M M365 commercial base — massive upsell runway
Balance sheet: $78.3B cash, $40.3B debt, ~$38B net cash; debt-to-equity 0.119; ROE 28.9%
2026 capex guided to ~$190B (vs $154.6B consensus), $25B from component inflation — margin compression risk (gross margin 67.6%, down ~140bp over 3 quarters)
10Y yield at 4.57% compresses earnings-yield spread (3.4% earnings yield vs 4.57% risk-free) — limits multiple re-expansion
UK CMA opened formal investigation May 14, 2026 into 'strategic market status' in business software; existing FTC and EU probes
Bill Ackman initiated 5.6M shares in Feb at ~21x forward; Gates Foundation completed exit of 7.7M shares ($3.2B); Third Point fully exited
OpenAI restructuring: revenue-sharing capped at $38B, IP licensing through 2032, IPO targeting Sept 2026 at >$1T valuation — contingent upside on ~27% stake

sources_cited.excerpt: Revenue from AI business surged 123% year-on-year, with an annual run rate of US$37 billion. Overall operating margin improved from 45.7% in Q3 2025 to 46.3% in Q3 2026

Nearly 60% of service customers have already moved to usage-based credits, and GitHub is similarly pivoting to a consumption model in June 2026 after enterprise subscribers nearly tripled year-on-year

Azure grew 40% in Q3 FY2026 and holds roughly 21–24% of the global cloud infrastructure market, behind AWS at ~28–30%... Only 20 million of Microsoft's 450 million M365 commercial subscribers pay for Copilot — about 4.4%

The selloff was not about earnings quality. It was about the disclosed 2026 calendar capex plan of approximately $190 billion, which exceeded analyst consensus of $154.6 billion by roughly $35 billion, and the explicit attribution of $25 billion of that figure to component price inflation rather than additional capacity
The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has completed its exit from Microsoft by selling its final 7.7 million shares worth $3.2 billion in Q1 2026

Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management has added Microsoft as a fourth 'Magnificent Seven' stock... Ackman built the Microsoft position in February when the stock traded at 21x forward earnings
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority opened a formal investigation on May 14 into whether Microsoft should be granted a 'strategic market status' in business software
Daniel Loeb's Third Point LLC significantly reshuffled its portfolio in Q1 2026, completely exiting positions in Microsoft
